question: The artistic and architectural style evident in the Bagh Caves of Madhya Pradesh, India, is predominantly associated with which of the following faiths? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Islam
Hinduism
Buddhism
Jainism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Buddhism

Explanation:
The Bagh Caves, located on the banks of the Bagh River in Madhya Pradesh, are associated with Buddhism. These caves were constructed around the 5th-6th century AD and consist of viharas (monastic residences) and a chaitya (prayer hall). The wall paintings found in the caves depict Buddhist themes such as the Jataka tales and scenes from the life of Buddha. The artistic style is heavily influenced by the Ajanta style of painting. Thus, the artistic and architectural style of the Bagh Caves is predominantly associated with Buddhism.

☛ State where Bagh Caves are located → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Who resided in these caves → Buddhist monks
☛ Painting style influencing Bagh Caves → Ajanta style
☛ What stories are depicted in Bagh Caves → Buddhist Jataka tales
question_hi: भारत के मध्य प्रदेश की बाघ गुफाओं में दिखाई देने वाली कलात्मक और वास्तुशिल्प शैली मुख्य रूप से निम्नलिखित में से किस धर्म से जुड़ी है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:
बाघ गुफाएँ मध्य प्रदेश के बाघ नदी के तट पर स्थित हैं और ये बौद्ध धर्म से संबंधित हैं। ये गुफाएँ लगभग 5वीं-6वीं शताब्दी ईस्वी में निर्मित मानी जाती हैं। इनमें विहार (भिक्षुओं के निवास) और चैत्य (प्रार्थना हॉल) शामिल हैं। गुफाओं की दीवारों पर बने चित्र बौद्ध धर्म से जुड़े हुए हैं और अजंता शैली से प्रभावित हैं। ये चित्र बौद्ध जातक कथाओं और बुद्ध के जीवन के दृश्यों का चित्रण करते हैं। इस प्रकार बाघ गुफाओं की कलात्मक और वास्तुशिल्प शैली मुख्य रूप से बौद्ध धर्म से जुड़ी है।

question: What is the ancient style of articles containing Egyptian symbols called?A. HieroglyphicsB. CuneiformC. HititeD. Zapotec (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 1)
options: A
C
D
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hieroglyphics

Explanation:
The ancient writing style of Egypt is known as Hieroglyphics. This pictographic writing system developed around 3200 BCE and included over 700 symbols. Hieroglyphs were used on temples, monuments, and papyrus. The discovery of the Rosetta Stone (1799) helped decipher this script. Cuneiform is the script of Mesopotamia, Hittite from Anatolia, and Zapotec from Mesoamerica.

☛ Time of origin of Hieroglyphics → Around 3200 BCE
☛ Stone that helped decipher Hieroglyphics → Rosetta Stone
☛ Cuneiform belongs to which civilization → Mesopotamia
☛ Where was Hittite script found → Anatolia

question: In which of the following countries, the Indus River does not flow?A. IndiaB. PakistanC. ChinaD. Afghanistan (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: D
C
A
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Afghanistan

Explanation:
The Indus River originates in Tibet (China), flows through India (Ladakh) and Pakistan, but does not flow through Afghanistan. It is one of the longest rivers in Asia, with a total length of about 3180 km. Its major tributaries include Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum. According to the Indus Water Treaty (1960), the water of eastern tributaries is allocated to India and the western ones to Pakistan. The river forms a large delta near Karachi in Pakistan. The Indus is also known for the ancient Indus Valley Civilization that flourished along its banks.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Origin of Indus River → Near Mansarovar in Tibet (China)
☛ Largest tributary of Indus → Chenab
☛ Year of Indus Water Treaty → 1960
☛ Location of Indus Delta → Pakistan (near Karachi)
☛ Length of Indus River → 3180 km

question: Name the Buddhist text that comprises rules for monks. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Tipitaka
Vinaya Pitaka
Sutta Pitaka
Abhidhamma Pitaka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vinaya Pitaka

Explanation:
In Buddhism, the Tripitaka is a collection of three major texts. The Vinaya Pitaka deals with the rules of discipline and conduct for monks and nuns. It contains detailed codes of conduct to be followed during spiritual practice. Among the other options, the Sutta Pitaka is a collection of the Buddha's discourses, while the Abhidhamma Pitaka is a philosophical and psychological text. The Tipitaka is the collective name for all three, not a single text. Hence, the Vinaya Pitaka comprises rules for monks.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ How many rules are in the Vinaya Pitaka? → 227 rules (for a full monk)
☛ How many sections are in the Vinaya Pitaka? → Three: Suttavibhanga, Khandhaka, Parivara
☛ Who founded the Buddhist Sangha? → Gautama Buddha
☛ How many Nikayas are in the Sutta Pitaka? → Five Nikayas
☛ How many books are in the Abhidhamma Pitaka? → Seven books

Explanation:
बौद्ध धर्म में त्रिपिटक तीन प्रमुख ग्रंथों का संग्रह है। विनय पिटक भिक्षुओं और भिक्षुणियों के लिए आचार-नियमों और अनुशासन से संबंधित है। इसमें साधना के दौरान पालन किए जाने वाले नियमों का विस्तृत वर्णन है। अन्य विकल्पों में, सुत्त पिटक बुद्ध के उपदेशों का संग्रह है, जबकि अभिधम्म पिटक दार्शनिक और मनोवैज्ञानिक ग्रंथ है। त्रिपिटक इन तीनों ग्रंथों का समूह है, न कि स्वयं एक ग्रंथ। अतः विनय पिटक में भिक्षुओं के लिए नियम हैं।

question: Which of the following is the correct chronological sequence of pre-historic period of human activities and civilization? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Palaeolithic Period, Mesolithic Period, Neolithic Period
Mesolithic Period×duplicate options found. English Question 1 options 3,4, , Neolithic Period, Palaeolithic Period
Metal age Period, Mesolithic Period, Palaeolithic Period
Neolithic Period, Mesolithic Period, Palaeolithic Period
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Palaeolithic Period, Mesolithic Period, Neolithic Period

Explanation:
The prehistoric period is divided into three main phases: Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age), Mesolithic (Middle Stone Age), and Neolithic (New Stone Age). The Palaeolithic period is the earliest, characterized by the use of crude stone tools and a hunter-gatherer lifestyle. It was followed by the Mesolithic period, which saw the development of microliths (small stone tools) and climatic changes. Finally, the Neolithic period marked the advent of agriculture, domestication of animals, and settled life. This chronological sequence reflects the gradual evolution of human civilization from simple tool use to organized farming communities.

☛ Beginning of agriculture and domestication → Neolithic period

☛ Period after Neolithic → Metal Age (Chalcolithic/Bronze Age)

question: In which state of India can we find the preserved Buddhist caves called 'Karla'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Karnataka
Maharashtra
Bihar
Uttar Pradesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Maharashtra

Explanation:
The Karla Caves are ancient Buddhist rock-cut caves located in the state of Maharashtra, India. Situated near Lonavala in the Pune district, these caves date back to the 2nd century BCE to the 5th century CE. The Karla Caves are renowned for their magnificent chaityagriha (prayer hall), which is one of the largest and best-preserved ancient cave temples in India. The cave complex features exquisite sculptures and inscriptions, reflecting both Hinayana and Mahayana traditions of Buddhism. The Karla Caves are a protected monument of national importance and attract numerous tourists and historians.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ When were the Karla Caves constructed? → 2nd century BCE to 5th century CE
☛ What is the main structure in Karla Caves? → Chaityagriha
☛ Which religion do the Karla Caves belong to? → Buddhism
☛ Which city is near the Karla Caves? → Lonavala

question: Who among the following was the first ruler who inscribed his message on stone surfaces for his subjects and officials? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (11/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Chandragupta Maurya
Ashoka
Harshavardhan
Chandragupta I
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ashoka

Explanation:
The tradition of inscribing messages on stone surfaces in India was begun by Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya dynasty. He had Edicts of Ashoka carved on rocks and pillars across his empire, containing messages on governance, morality, and compassion. These inscriptions were written in Prakrit language using Brahmi script. Ashoka's edicts provide valuable insights into the extent and administration of the Mauryan empire. Chandragupta Maurya, Harshavardhan, and Chandragupta I did not use stone inscriptions for royal messages.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ In which language are Ashoka's edicts? → Prakrit
☛ Which script was used in Ashoka's edicts? → Brahmi
☛ Which edict of Ashoka mentions the Kalinga War? → 13th Rock Edict

question: Where, in India, would you find rock paintings dating back to the stone age? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/02/2021) Shift 1)

question: Which statement from the given options is NOT correct? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (17/02/2021) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following ages did NOT fall under the three main divisions of the Stone Age? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (12/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Eneolithic
Palaeolithic
Mesolithic
Neolithic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Eneolithic

Explanation:
The three main divisions of the Stone Age are Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic. These divisions are based on the evolution of stone tool technology and changes in human lifestyle. The Eneolithic (or Chalcolithic) period came after the Stone Age, marking the beginning of the use of copper and bronze. It is part of the Copper Age and transitions into the Bronze Age, not the Stone Age. Therefore, it does not fall under the three main divisions of the Stone Age.

question: In the state Emblem of India there is a quote saying 'Satyameva Jayate,' which is inscribed in Devanagari script. This quote has been taken from: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 1)

question: Asoka, arguably the most famous ruler of early India, conquered Kalinga. He was the grandson of _____. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (13/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Chandragupta Maurya
Samudragupta
Prabhavati Gupta
Chandragupta II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chandragupta Maurya

Explanation:
Asoka was the third emperor of the Mauryan dynasty. He was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya, who founded the Mauryan Empire. Asoka ruled approximately from 268 to 232 BCE. After the Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE), he renounced violence and embraced Buddhism. Asoka's edicts and pillars are important sources of his reign. Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of Chanakya, defeated the Nanda dynasty and laid the foundation of the Mauryan Empire. Asoka is known for spreading Dhamma (righteousness). He appointed Dhamma Mahamatras (officers). His son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra propagated Buddhism in Sri Lanka.

question: Which of the following statements is true about the Sutta Pitaka? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/03/2021) Shift 1)

It is about the rules and regulations for those who joined the Buddhist monastic order.
It is the biography of the Buddha.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It deals with the conversation between the ruler of Magadha and the Buddha.

Explanation:
The Sutta Pitaka is one of the three main texts of Buddhism, known as the Tipitaka. It contains the discourses of the Buddha and his disciples. Specifically, within the Sutta Pitaka, the Digha Nikaya includes suttas like the 'Samannaphala Sutta', which describes a conversation between the ruler of Magadha, Ajatashatru, and the Buddha. This text was originally written in the Pali language and is preserved in the Theravada tradition. Other options are incorrect: the first is false because it claims the text was written in Sri Lanka, whereas it was originally composed in India; the third option relates to the Vinaya Pitaka, which deals with monastic rules; the fourth is false because the biography of the Buddha is found in texts like the Buddhacharita, not the Sutta Pitaka.

question: At which of the following places did Gautam Buddha attain enlightenment? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/03/2021) Shift 1)

question: The most common Harappan seals were _________ in shape. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: square
rectangular
circular
hexagonal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is square

Explanation:
The most common Harappan seals were square in shape, made primarily from stone like steatite. These seals typically featured engravings of animals such as the unicorn (one-horned bull), tiger, elephant, rhinoceros, and occasionally deities. They were used for trade and administrative purposes to indicate ownership. Over 2000 seals have been discovered, inscribed with the Harappan script (pictographic). These seals provide significant evidence of trade activities, social structure, and religious beliefs of the Harappan civilization, which flourished during the Bronze Age.

question: What is the height of the Allahabad pillar which bears inscriptions associated with Samudragupta? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (19/03/2021) Shift 2)

question: The worship of images of Buddha became an important tradition in: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Hinayana
Mahayana
Vajrayana
Nyingma
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahayana

Explanation:
The worship of images of Buddha became an important tradition in Mahayana Buddhism. Mahayana, meaning 'Great Vehicle', is a major branch of Buddhism. In Mahayana, Buddha is revered as a divine being and emphasis is placed on the concept of bodhisattvas who work for the liberation of others. In contrast, Hinayana Buddhism places less emphasis on image worship and focuses more on individual salvation. Vajrayana is tantric Buddhism which evolved from Mahayana, and Nyingma is a sect of Tibetan Buddhism. Mahayana popularized image worship, making Buddhism accessible to the common people. This tradition included the creation of Buddha statues and stupas for veneration.

question: On the bank of which river was Harappa Civilisation situated? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Bhogwa river
Sindhu river
Satluj river
Ravi river
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ravi river

Explanation:
The Harappan civilisation is a major site of the Indus Valley Civilisation, located in present-day Punjab province of Pakistan. The city was situated on the banks of the Ravi River, one of the five major tributaries of the Indus River. Harappa was discovered in 1921 by Dayaram Sahni. This civilisation flourished around 2500 BCE and is renowned for its urban planning, drainage system, and seals. At Harappa, a large granary, bronze statues, and bead-making factories have been found. The Ravi River is mentioned as Iravati in Vedic literature. The Indus Valley Civilisation is also known as the Harappan Civilisation after this site.

question: The concept of Bodhisattva is associated with:  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Mahayana Buddhism
Jainism
Hinyana Buddhism
Sikhism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahayana Buddhism

Explanation:
The concept of Bodhisattva is associated with Mahayana Buddhism. Mahayana, meaning 'Great Vehicle', is a major branch of Buddhism. A Bodhisattva is an enlightened being who postpones Nirvana to help all sentient beings achieve liberation, guided by compassion and bodhicitta. The Bodhisattva path emphasizes the practice of the paramitas (perfections: generosity, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, wisdom). In contrast, Hinayana (Theravada) focuses on becoming an Arhat, not a Bodhisattva. Jainism and Sikhism do not have the concept of Bodhisattva. Thus, the Bodhisattva ideal is central to Mahayana Buddhism, distinguishing it from other traditions.

Explanation:
बोधिसत्व की अवधारणा महायान बौद्ध धर्म से जुड़ी है। महायान का अर्थ है 'बड़ा वाहन', जो बौद्ध धर्म की एक प्रमुख शाखा है। इसमें बोधिसत्व वह व्यक्ति है जो बुद्धत्व प्राप्त करने से पहले सभी प्राणियों के उद्धार के लिए करुणा और बोधिचित्त का पालन करता है। महायान में बोधिसत्व मार्ग को सर्वोच्च माना जाता है, जो पारमिताओं (दान, शील, क्षांति, वीर्य, ध्यान, प्रज्ञा) के अभ्यास द्वारा बुद्धत्व की ओर अग्रसर होता है। इसके विपरीत, हीनयान या थेरवाद में अर्हत बनने पर जोर दिया जाता है, न कि बोधिसत्व बनने पर। जैन धर्म और सिख धर्म में बोधिसत्व की अवधारणा नहीं मिलती। इस प्रकार, बोधिसत्व महायान बौद्ध धर्म का केंद्रीय सिद्धांत है।
